patch.value: The transport is an interface with a filesystem implementation, not a network protocol yet

Phase 3 defines fetch, push and clone against a Transport interface and ships one implementation that reaches a repository through the filesystem. That is the whole of what the distribution logic needs to be correct: negotiation, fast-forward checking and compare-and-swap ref updates are properties of the algorithm, not of the wire. Committing to a network protocol now would fix a serialization format before the forge phase has said what a served repository exposes, and the two would then have to agree retroactively. The interface is the commitment; a served implementation lands with the forge.

fetch, push and clone are written against the Transport interface and never touch a filesystem path directly; adding a second implementation requires no change to the sync algorithms; the decision records why a network transport is deferred rather than leaving it as an unexplained gap

author: harness:claude-code

patch.value: Shipped in the distribution tranche: remotes, transport interface, fetch/push/clone with reachability negotiation, 100/100/100 coverage.
